answer.rationale: With the line at 94% committed volume and zero buffer, and the primary contract lapsing in 14 days without auto-renewal, switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor (memory_c2) carries known SLA-miss risk that could break delivery under a no-slack schedule	too dangerous given the objective of not increasing delivery risk. The incumbent already provides stable integration and on-time delivery (memory_c1), and prior renegotiations (memory_c4) and multi-year commitments (memory_c6) recovered margin and cut unit cost without narrowing service scope	directly addressing the 18% spend-cut mandate. Deferring (memory_c5) was validated only for a non-critical, month-to-month-eligible service, not a critical line facing imminent contract expiry, so it's not a safe analog here. Adding a second source (memory_c3) is valuable for shortage resilience but doesn't address the urgent expiring contract or the cost mandate this cycle. I verified c4 and c6 because they carry the load of the cost-reduction claim central to this decision and are the least-recently reaffirmed; c1 and c2 are more recent/self-evident in their caveats. Given only one decision slot, negotiating renewed terms with the incumbent best balances cost reduction and delivery-risk avoidance, while leaving second-sourcing and vendor-switch options open for the next review.
